unit.title: Formal & Literary Register
unit.subtitle: Elevating your Spanish for emails, essays, and formal speech

grammar.title: Know when — and how — to elevate your Spanish
grammar.intro: At C1 you must shift register on demand. In a formal email, essay, or address you swap everyday verbs for elevated ones (comenzar for empezar, adquirir for comprar, solicitar for pedir), you deploy set courtesy formulas (le ruego que, quedo a la espera de), and you even use the future or conditional to hedge a conjecture politely. The skill is not just knowing these forms — it's sensing when the situation calls for them and dropping the colloquialisms.

sections.heading: Elevated verbs replace everyday ones
sections.body: Formal Spanish prefers a more precise, latinate verb. In an essay or professional email, choose the left-hand column. Using the colloquial version in a formal register reads as careless; using the formal one in a chat with friends reads as stiff — register is about fit.

ex.en: The company acquired a new headquarters.
I request that you review the file.

sections.heading: Formulaic courtesy phrases
sections.body: Formal correspondence runs on fixed phrases. Le ruego que (+ subjunctive) softens a request; quedo a la espera de closes a letter awaiting a reply; agradezco de antemano thanks in advance; en lo que respecta a frames a topic; cabe destacar/señalar que foregrounds a key point in an essay. Note le ruego que takes the subjunctive: le ruego que disculpe.

ex.es: Le ruego que me disculpe por la demora.
ex.en: I kindly ask you to excuse the delay.

ex.es: Quedo a la espera de su respuesta.
ex.en: I look forward to your reply.

sections.heading: Future & conditional of probability
sections.body: Spanish uses the future to conjecture about the present ('it must be / probably is') and the conditional to conjecture about the past ('it must have been / probably was'). In formal registers this is an elegant way to hedge without adding 'probablemente'. Serán las cinco = it's probably five; Serían las cinco = it was probably five.

ex.en: He isn't answering; he must be in a meeting.
Some thousand people probably attended the event.

sections.heading: When to elevate — and what to drop
sections.body: Elevate for formal emails, essays, applications, and public speech; stay colloquial with friends. When elevating, drop fillers and slang: replace o sea with es decir, un montón de with numerosos, vale with de acuerdo, and address the reader as usted. The goal is a consistent tone, not a single fancy word dropped into casual text.

ex.en: Numerous applications were received this quarter.
I agree with what has been set out.

takeaways: Elevated verbs: comenzar, adquirir, solicitar, mostrar/exponer, precisar.
Formal formulas: le ruego que (+ subj.), quedo a la espera de, cabe destacar que.
Future = present conjecture (Serán las cinco); conditional = past conjecture (Serían las cinco).
Elevating means dropping slang: es decir not 'o sea', de acuerdo not 'vale', usted not tú.

mistakes.w: Le ruego que revisa el expediente.
mistakes.r: Le ruego que revise el expediente.
mistakes.why: 'Le ruego que' triggers the subjunctive: revise, not the indicative revisa.

mistakes.w: Estimado cliente: vale, un montón de gracias.
mistakes.r: Estimado cliente: de acuerdo, muchas gracias.
mistakes.why: In a formal email, drop colloquialisms like 'vale' and 'un montón de'; use 'de acuerdo' and 'muchas'.
The future of probability already means 'probably'; adding 'probablemente' is redundant.

exercises.prompt: Le ruego que me ___ por la demora en la respuesta.
exercises.prompt_en: I kindly ask you to excuse me for the delay in replying.
exercises.no: 'Le ruego que' triggers the subjunctive: 'disculpe', not the indicative 'disculpa'.

exercises.prompt: En el informe: la empresa ___ una nueva sede en Madrid.
exercises.prompt_en: In the report: the company acquired new headquarters in Madrid.
exercises.no: In formal prose, the elevated verb is 'adquirió'; the others are colloquial.

exercises.prompt: Build: "I look forward to your reply. I thank you in advance."
exercises.no: Use the formal sign-off 'Quedo a la espera de su respuesta. Agradezco de antemano.' — the colloquial 'vale' has no place here.

exercises.prompt: No contesta el teléfono; ___ reunido en este momento. (estar, conjetura)
exercises.prompt_en: He isn't answering the phone; he must be in a meeting right now.
exercises.hint: Future of 'estar' used to conjecture about the present.
exercises.no: To conjecture about the present, use the future of probability: 'estará' (he must be).

exercises.prompt: Match each colloquial word to its formal equivalent.

exercises.tts: Cabe destacar que la propuesta resultó viable.
accepted: cabe destacar que la propuesta resulto viable
exercises.translation: It is worth noting that the proposal proved viable.
exercises.ok: ¡Correcto! “Cabe destacar que la propuesta resultó viable.”
exercises.no: It was: “Cabe destacar que la propuesta resultó viable.” (It is worth noting that the proposal proved viable.)

exercises.scenario: Replying to a client's formal complaint email ✉️

lines.speaker: Cliente
lines.es: Llevo dos semanas sin recibir el pedido. Necesito una solución.
lines.en: I've gone two weeks without receiving the order. I need a solution.

options.text: Le ruego que disculpe la demora; en breve le enviaremos una compensación.
Vale, tranqui, ya te lo mando cuando pueda, ¿okey?
Le ruego que disculpa el retraso, un montón de gracias.

exercises.no: Keep it formal and grammatical: option b is slang; option c uses the indicative 'disculpa' after 'le ruego que'.

exercises.say: Quedo a la espera de su respuesta.
exercises.en: I look forward to your reply.
exercises.no: Almost — tap “Hear it”, then match the rhythm of “Quedo a la espera de su respuesta.”
